newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Volker 1996 profit seen sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Volker 1996 profit seen sharply up.

text.p: Dutch builder Volker Stevin is expected to book a sharply higher 1996 net profit from ordinary operations this week, buoyed by a healthy Dutch infrastructure market and a low tax bill.
Analysts are forecasting the leading Dutch road builder will on Friday post a full-year net from ordinary operations of 64 to 77 million guilders, with a consensus forecast at 68 million.
In 1995 Volker Stevin posted ordinary net of 57.2 million.
"Volker Stevin lost very few working days in the second half and will have forged ahead," predicted Paul Verbraeken, construction analyst with ING Barings.
He said the builder, which derives some 80-85 percent of its turnover from the Netherlands, would continue to benefit from an expanding market in road and rail building.
"The second-half earnings upturn will come from autonomous growth, while Volker Stevin's tax bill for the year will be lower," Verbraeken said.
The builder made no provisions against tax in the first half, as it still had substantial tax losses to carry forward.
"Volker Stevin's markets are in good shape and future prospects are good," agreed Sven Smit of Bank Labouchere.

Smit, who rates the stock a "Buy", is forecasting full-year ordinary net of 68 million guilders, reflecting an earnings acceleration in the second half after the harsh winter braked first-half profit growth.
"First-half figures at Volker Stevin say very little about the full year, as the company only books completed projects," Smit said.

Future prospects were also bright, given that the bulk of contracts for major infrastructure projects such as the Betuwe freight-only link to Germany and the high-speed rail link would be awarded in 1998, he added.
Suez Nederland's Fernand de Boer praised the builder's recent acquisition of part of the maintenance and breakdown activities of Dutch Rail NS.
"These will engender a better spread of cash flow," he said, adding Volker already had the required certification to undertake NS projects.
Analysts were also upbeat on Volker Stevin's position in the Dutch housing and general construction market, which accounted for just under half of total turnover in the first 1996 half.
"Volker tends to take on multi-year projects and because it is big enough to offer an integrated approach it has an advantage over the mid-sized builders," Smit said.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
